How bees measure distance

Honeybees measure how far they have flown by the amount of image motion they see, a signal called optic flow. In tunnels with patterned walls, bees overestimate distance, and their dances report a longer flight than they really made.

This means the waggle dance reports the visual experience of the flight rather than an absolute distance, and dances from different landscapes can encode the same distance differently. Recruits still find the food because they experience the same landscape on their way.

The finding explains why dance calibration differs between colonies living in open fields and colonies living in dense forest.
